title: Domain, Data Transfer Object (DTO), and record — allocation-aware
hook: Domain models enforce business rules. Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) cross API boundaries. Records fit immutable DTOs with value equality — but every mapping and copy is an allocation you should notice on CSV import and high-traffic Redis paths.

blocks.text: Domain entities live in the core layer with invariants — Order cannot ship without lines. DTOs are serializable shapes for HTTP, queues, and cache values — often records. Mapping between them (manual, Mapster, source generator) allocates. For hot paths, read-only structs or span-parsed rows may replace heap DTOs — module 17 CSV topic.

entries.plainDefinition: Type designed to carry data across a boundary without behavior.
entries.example: public record UserResponse(int Id, string Email);

entries.plainDefinition: Object with business rules and invariants, not tied to transport format.
entries.example: class Order { public void Ship() { /* validates state */ } }

entries.plainDefinition: Converting between domain and DTO representations.
entries.example: new UserResponse(user.Id, user.Email) — allocates new record.

blocks.text: Exposing domain entities directly from EF Core APIs couples persistence to HTTP and causes over-fetching. Over-mapping — domain to DTO to view model on every Redis hit — doubles allocations. CSV import of millions of rows should stream DTOs or parse into structs, not materialize List<ExpandoObject>.

blocks.title: Layering rule
blocks.body: Controllers and message handlers speak DTOs. Domain services speak domain types. Map at the edge once.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: EF entities returned from minimal APIs. Triple mapping domain→DTO→view. class DTO for million-row import when struct suffices. Giant DTOs cached in Redis.

interviewTakeaways: Domain has behavior; DTOs cross boundaries; records suit immutable DTOs.
Map at the edge once; avoid mapping chains on hot paths.
record struct can reduce allocations for bulk import rows.
commonPitfalls: Allocating new DTO on every cache hit when reference could be reused safely.
Ignoring DTO size in Redis memory.
